claim: a personal result (fifty bucks into five grand by folding more) that no fact supports
honest: claimed winnings: LlamaPoker has no wins to brag about
helping: does not offer money back or push a losing player to play more

claim: 'every poker app review says the river is rigged' is a claim about every review with no fact behind it; the 35% itself matches flush-river
a second-person scene; a table folding to the tight player's rare raise is common table behaviour
helping: names a frustration to explain it

claim: wait-bb (9.75 bb) is an average over a 39-hand average wait; 'each one has already cost you' says it as a certainty
helping: explains a cost, no offer to win it back

claim: 16% is gutshot-river (16.47%) with its conditions, flop to river; 'half right' is answerable from that chance
second-person scene; 'proves nothing' follows from aces losing 14% against a random hand (aa-lose-1)
honest: no brag; luck not used as an excuse
helping: names a loss to explain it

claim: 35% by the river from the flop matches flush-river (34.97%); the cost line gives no figure and the turn-only fact (19.57%) lets the reel answer it
a feeling put to the viewer in the second person ('it feels like it always does'), not a claim to back
helping: names a loss to explain it

claim: 14% matches aa-lose-1 (14.47%) with its conditions: preflop all-in, one random hand
honest: luck is named only to be denied

claim: follows from aa-lose-once-in-20 (95.62%): enough all-ins and a loss is all but certain; no figure is misquoted
1 in 3 is flush-river (34.97%) rounded, with its conditions said: from the flop, seeing both cards
1 in 39 matches premium-every and keeps 'on average'; 'a bill' is the blinds paid while waiting (wait-bb) with no figure overstated
85% matches aa-vs-1 (85.26%) with its conditions: all-in preflop, one random hand
'it was supposed to happen' is unbacked: aces lose to one random hand 14% of the time, which makes the loss possible, not expected
the hook asks how often aces lose to ace-king by running kings; the facts only cover aces against random hands, so the reel cannot answer it
35% by the river from the flop matches flush-river; 'you only remember the misses' is a memory put to the viewer, not a claim to back
table behaviour any regular would agree with: a player who rarely raises gets credit when he does; no cost, odds or frequency asserted
honest: luck is named only to be denied

claim: wrong number and wrong population: against four random hands aces hold 55.88% of the pot (aa-vs-4); 85% is their share against one
'most players call that fold a mistake' and 'most of the time it's the right one' are both unbacked; no fact covers bet sizes or pot odds
79% (aa-lose-once-in-10) holds only heads-up against a random hand; 'shove aces ten times' says it as if it held for any all-in
'wins it back by Friday' is a result no fact supports
honest: promises a result LlamaPoker cannot truthfully promise
helping: offers winning the money back and speaks to someone who just lost a stack

claim: blinds are paid in two seats per orbit (orbit-bb), so 'paying for every hand he folds' states a cost that holds only in some seats as if in all; 'losing slowly' is unbacked too
honest: luck is named only to be denied

claim: beliefs put to the viewer in the second person, which the viewer accepts or rejects; no odds asserted

c04.why: Every regular has lived this exact evening, and the line stops on the sting without explaining it, so the viewer stays for the why.

c09.why: It names the beat a stranger replays in their own head and admits the feeling before any number arrives.

c25.why: A then-and-now arc any player recognises in themselves, self-mocking and finished in two short beats.

c07.why: A specific, painful hand followed by a flat verdict against what the viewer concluded from it.

c19.why: A lived frustration with a tease that the table read you, which the reel has to pay off.

c11.why: It turns a boast into a tell in one sentence and dares the viewer to check their own record.

c18.why: It opens on the viewer's own complaint and turns the blame onto what they paid, though the number sits in the middle.

c12.why: It quotes the complaint in the viewer's own words and answers it at once, but ends on a fact rather than a stake.

c14.why: The last two sentences attack a habit tight players are proud of, but the opening is a statistic.

c10.why: The denial of luck is a stance, but the turn only arrives in the third sentence after a statistic.
